$comment: Ceilings for every shipped wasm artifact, read by `cargo xtask size` against the cargo artifact `cargo xtask dist wasm` ships (the release build with remapped paths, before wasm-bindgen and wasm-opt). Shrink-only: a ceiling more than the headroom above its artifact fails until lowered with `cargo xtask size --update`; raising one is a hand edit, and its reason says why the growth is worth it.

whiteboard-wasm.reason: Production exports only, measured at the cargo artifact: 1260974 bytes, the shipped (wasm-bindgen stripped) module 784341. What the artifact carries: abi_version, the one-call-per-layout routing export edge_route_layout over the router, anchor pass, repair, crossing sweep and side-choice search (production code the default routing will run), the OKF codec behind okf_parse and okf_serialize, the JSON Canvas codec behind json_canvas_parse and json_canvas_serialize, and facet_bucket_check, the facet write over the contract interpreter, the plugin loader and registry and the visual plugin's checks and embedded files (the daemon's only write validator, under owner decision q41). The per-module layer-2 test exports (the det_* batches, edge_route_on_grid, and each edge module's edge_* export) moved behind the `oracle-surface` cargo feature, built only for the test lanes by `cargo xtask dist wasm --oracle`: that took 102331 bytes off the cargo artifact (1363305 before) and 51003 off the shipped module (835344 before). What remains of the edge code is reached by edge_route_layout, so it stays. Every released build ships this artifact (the npm tarball, the Docker image and the web site) while the default routing stays TypeScript, so only `differential` and `rust` load it.
